1140.headline: Where this game is in its run

696.body:
"Monopoly 200X" has had no $5 million top prize claimed since we started watching it. Everyday prizes keep getting claimed, and fewer tickets are left each day. The number of tickets printed is fixed. Each day without a top prize claim leaves those prizes among fewer tickets.

The numbers for "Monopoly 200X" will change a little by tomorrow, and this page will change with them.
696.headline: Over a month, no top prize claimed

762.body:
Of the unclaimed prize money on "Billion", about three-quarters is in wins under $5,000. The game is a game that pays many small prizes and few large ones. That is neither good nor bad, only how it was designed. Choose the kind of game that fits the win you want.

How far "Billion" is through its run does not decide anything by itself. It changes how closely to look at the other numbers.

Tomorrow's count on "Billion" will be a little different. The game sells every day, and this page keeps track.
762.headline: How the prize money is divided

827.body:
"50th Anniversary" is in the last part of its run, with about a quarter of its tickets still unsold. Late in a run, a game is worth a look when prizes outlast tickets. Early on, the prize design matters most. Here, a larger share of the top prizes is left than of the tickets, which is a good sign.

If "50th Anniversary" is your usual pick, check this page often. The prize counts change even when the ticket looks the same.
827.headline: How much has sold

847.body:
Before you buy "Bingo 50X", know that its $500,000 top prize is gone. The game still pays many smaller prizes, but the biggest one left is $100,000. That is less than the ticket advertises, though still a sizable prize.

Today's free summary of "Bingo 50X" ends here. Every number behind it is on this page.
847.headline: All four top prizes claimed

891.body:
"Cash Explosion 25X" has 83,440 prizes of $5 still unclaimed, which is its most common win. Just below the top prize is the $10,000 prize, with one left. The full count for every prize level is listed below.

Everything above about "Cash Explosion 25X" comes from the Ohio Lottery's own published numbers. We only do the counting.
